jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas, or New York City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Growth here is not bought — no paid media, no ad spend, no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM or relationship-tracking user; logging relationships, first-contact attribution, follow-ups, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or would return or relocate to, one of these regions where you already have a deep local relationship network: Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas, or New York City
Available to host on weekday evenings and weekends as a regular rhythm, with local travel
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

We need someone with founder-level energy and credibility. Someone who understands that the best ideas mean nothing without relentless execution. Someone who can turn a sharp point of view into a school parents can’t stop talking about—and students can’t wait to attend.

Design, validate, and scale a high-performance gifted school model—starting with a single prototype campus and expanding to a national network.

Built and scaled a high-impact venture from scratch (bonus if it involved physical operations or education). We are talking about at least 1M USD yearly revenue owned by you
Deep, personal understanding of gifted students—whether through family, professional experience, or lived reality
AI First mentality — Inclination to prioritize AI as the default solution for problem-solving, decision-making and work output generation at scale.

new_jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas, or New York City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Growth here is not bought — no paid media, no ad spend, no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM or relationship-tracking user; logging relationships, first-contact attribution, follow-ups, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or would return or relocate to, one of these regions where you already have a deep local relationship network: Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas, or New York City
Available to host on weekday evenings and weekends as a regular rhythm, with local travel
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.
